newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street surges at open, NYSE sets curbs.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street surges at open, NYSE sets curbs.

text.p: Wall Street stocks roared higher at the market open on Tuesday, as bargain hunters, reassured over Japan's stance on U.S. government bonds, rushed back into the market after yesteday's steep sell-off .

The Dow Jones Industrial Average, which had been hit yesterday after Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto made comments suggesting a potential Japanese sale of U.S. government bonds, surged 64.46 points or nearly one percent to 7668.04. The New York Stock Exchange set curbs on index arbitrage trading three minutes after the market open.
Nasdaq gain nearly 10 points to trade at around 1444.
